ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: On the left side of the figure is a benzene ring, and there are two adjacent (ortho) substituents on the benzene ring; one substituent is labeled NH2, and the other is a -CH2- extending from the benzene ring followed by a carbonyl group C=O, then followed by a carboxylic acid group C(=O)OH. The figure also has curved arrows indicating electron transfer, and an H+ not covalently connected to the main body is shown in the upper right. Reasoning: The question requires ignoring the arrows, so only transcribe the atoms and connection relationships. The benzene ring bearing -NH2 and -CH2-C(=O)-C(=O)OH at ortho positions can be written as Nc1ccccc1CC(=O)C(=O)O; the separate proton is appended as an unconnected component as .[H+].

method.method_draft: Ignore all curved arrows and transcribe only atoms/connectivity. Identify the benzene ring with adjacent substituents: one substituent is -NH2 and the ortho substituent is -CH2-C(=O)-C(=O)OH. Write the aromatic ring as Nc1ccccc1 with the side chain attached at the ring-closure carbon, giving Nc1ccccc1CC(=O)C(=O)O. Since the image also shows a separate proton H+ not covalently bonded, append it as a disconnected component: Nc1ccccc1CC(=O)C(=O)O.[H+].
